title: CLI entry point does not exist: mdoutline.py has no main/argparse; every spec CLI claim is untestable
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 227c19c (Python 3.14.6, Linux, repo /home/lpaydat/workspace/mdoutline).

CLAIM: spec 'mdoutline NOTES.md — prints the outline' + Implementation Decisions 'single module mdoutline.py ... CLI surface frozen as specced: optional positional file argument, --max-depth N, --numbers; errors to stderr, exit 1/0'.

ACTUAL: mdoutline.py (136 lines) contains only extract_headings() and render_outline(). No main(), no argparse, no [project.scripts] in pyproject.toml.

EVIDENCE:
- which mdoutline -> rc 1 (not installed anywhere)
- python mdoutline.py --help -> exit 0, ZERO output (module is a silent no-op)
- echo '# Hi' | python mdoutline.py -> no stdout
- grep -c subprocess tests/test_mdoutline.py -> 0 (all 33 tests are library unit tests; spec Testing Decisions promised subprocess CLI-behaviour tests)

REPRO:
  git checkout 227c19c && python mdoutline.py --help; echo $?   # 0, no output
  echo '# Hi' | python mdoutline.py                              # nothing

IMPACT: The product's only user-facing surface (the CLI) does not exist at this HEAD. Ticket-01 (t_8e2a4417, done) scoped its dev card t_467e2f11 to the library only; the CLI ACs from ticket-01 (file arg, stdin fallback, missing-file exit 1, subprocess tests) remain undelivered and untracked by any card.

SEVERITY: Critical/P1 — blocks shipping the spec's core promise. Route: debugger + tech-lead (ticket-01 remainder needs re-scoping into a tracked card).

title: make install / pip install -e . fails: invalid build backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend'
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 227c19c (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM: Makefile target 'install: pip install -e ".[dev]"' (the documented dev bootstrap) and ADR-001 packaging posture.

ACTUAL: pyproject.toml [build-system] build-backend = 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' — module does not exist.

EVIDENCE:
  source .venv/bin/activate && make install
  -> pip._vendor.pyproject_hooks._impl.BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'
  -> make: *** [Makefile:4: install] Error 2

Workaround used by QA: pip install pytest ruff directly (works; make check then green).

FIX: build-backend = 'setuptools.build_meta' (or 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__' — the real legacy path; the declared name garbles both).

SEVERITY: Important/P2 — breaks the standard install path for every fresh clone. Route: debugger.

comments.author: lpaydat
comments.text: Verified fixed by 72f6be4 in QA re-test t_68b2f25e: build-backend=setuptools.build_meta; make install green in fresh venv AND non-editable pip install . green.

title: make install fails: pyproject build-backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' does not exist
description:
QA re-test t_6b5e5c59 @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip 26.1.2).

CLAIM TESTED: scaffold ticket T1 (566d0c1) ships a working dev install path (Makefile: 'install: pip install -e ".[dev]"').

ACTUAL: 'pip install -e ".[dev]"' aborts with BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'. pyproject.toml:3 declares build-backend = 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' — no such module exists in setuptools. The correct legacy backend is 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__'.

REPRO: cd /home/lpaydat/workspace/mdoutline && make install
-> BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'

ROOT-CAUSE PROOF: copied repo to a scratch dir, changed only the backend string to 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__', reran 'python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"' -> success (exit 0, import mdoutline OK).

IMPACT: documented build path dead for any fresh contributor; ticket 3 (CLI entry point / packaging) will hit this immediately. Workaround exists (run pytest directly; conftest.py puts repo root on sys.path — 33 tests pass without install). Severity Important/P2, not Critical: core library functionality unaffected.

FIX: pyproject.toml:3 -> build-backend = 'setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__' (or plain 'setuptools.build_meta'). Note: conftest.py + spec say 'no packaging beyond what pytest needs', so dropping the build-backend entirely is also viable — dev decision.

NOTE: no epic bead exists in this repo's beads DB (same as prior cycle t_543b747a noted) — no parent to link. Origin card: t_6b5e5c59.

title: Traceback on closed stdout: mdoutline FILE >&- crashes with AttributeError NoneType
description:
QA re-test t_40226fa7 @ 36d2b75 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness): CLI should degrade with a clean one-line stderr error when stdout is closed, like native tools.

ACTUAL: 'mdoutline FILE >&-' prints a Python traceback to stderr and exits 1:
  File mdoutline.py line 182 in main -> sys.stdout.write(outline)
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'
(sys.stdout is None when fd 1 is closed; the new BrokenPipeError trap does not catch AttributeError/OSError.)

REPRO: mdoutline any.md >&- ; echo rc=0

NATIVE COMPARISON: cat any.md >&- -> 'cat: standard output: Bad file descriptor', rc 1 (clean one-liner).

FIX DIRECTION: guard sys.stdout is None alongside the existing sys.stdin is None check; catch OSError around the write and emit 'mdoutline: cannot write to standard output: <reason>'.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — exotic edge (daemonized/misused fd), cosmetic traceback noise, no data loss. Same write-path robustness class as mdoutline-e52. Route: debugger.

title: ENOSPC on stdout (>/dev/full) prints full traceback instead of clean one-line error
description:
QA re-test t_40226fa7 @ 36d2b75 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness / graceful degradation): on write failure such as disk full, CLI should print one clean stderr line and exit nonzero, like native tools.

ACTUAL: 'mdoutline big.md >/dev/full' prints a multi-line traceback and exits 1:
  File mdoutline.py line 182 in main -> sys.stdout.write(outline)
  OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
The new BrokenPipeError handler catches only BrokenPipeError; OSError 28 propagates as a traceback. (Note: line-buffered write surfaced here immediately; small outputs can also fail at flush.)

REPRO: python3 -c "open('/tmp/big.md','w').write(''.join('# H'+str(i)+chr(10) for i in range(200000)))"; mdoutline /tmp/big.md >/dev/full

NATIVE COMPARISON: cat /tmp/big.md >/dev/full -> 'cat: standard output: No space left on device', rc 1 (clean one-liner).

FIX DIRECTION: broaden the write-path except clause to OSError (handling BrokenPipeError's SIGPIPE-style exit first), print one-line error, return 1.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — edge condition, cosmetic traceback noise + correct rc; real-world disk-full scenario for scripted use. Same write-path class as mdoutline-e52. Route: debugger.

title: BrokenPipeError traceback leaks to stderr when consumer closes pipe early (mdoutline FILE | head)
description:
QA re-test t_1075174f @ 72f6be4 (Python 3.14.5, Linux, pip-installed console script).

CLAIM (implicit CLI robustness / Unix idiom): 'mdoutline FILE | head -n' should degrade silently like standard CLIs.

ACTUAL: When the downstream consumer exits before mdoutline finishes writing, mdoutline raises an unhandled BrokenPipeError: traceback is printed to stderr and exit code is 1.

REPRO (deterministic):
  python3 -c "open('/tmp/big.md','w').write(''.join(f'#{chr(35)*(i%6+1)} Heading {i}'+chr(10) for i in range(200000)))"
  mdoutline /tmp/big.md | head -2
  -> Traceback ... File 'mdoutline.py', line 170, in main
     sys.stdout.write(outline)
     BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
  -> PIPESTATUS[0] = 1

OUTPUT CORRECTNESS: the lines head() consumed are delivered correctly; only failure mode is noise + nonzero rc.

FIX SUGGESTION: wrap the write in try/except BrokenPipeError (exit 0 or 141), and/or devnull-dup stdout before interpreter exit to suppress the secondary flush error.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic traceback in a common pipe idiom; no data loss. Route: debugger.
close_reason: Fixed by 36d2b75. QA re-test t_40226fa7 verified: 0-byte stderr, consumer lines delivered, SIGPIPE-style rc 13 (matches native 'seq' at 141 family — documented). Distinct stdout closed-fd and ENOSPC edges split into mdoutline-0s9/v0f.

title: UTF-8 BOM on first line silently drops the file's first heading
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 227c19c (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM: spec 'It must work on real-world Markdown'.

OBSERVED (exploratory, beyond spec): extract_headings(['\ufeff# Title', '## A']) -> [(2, 'A')]. The BOM prefixes the '#', so the line does not start with '#' and is not recognized as a heading — the file's h1 silently disappears from the outline. Common for Windows-authored files saved as UTF-8-with-BOM.

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['\ufeff# Title', '## A']))"

FIX DIRECTION: strip a leading '\ufeff' before the ATX scan (or open files with encoding='utf-8-sig' once the CLI exists).

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic, real-world-frequency edge. Route: debugger.
close_reason: Fixed by 36d2b75 (utf-8-sig on file+stdin). QA re-test t_40226fa7 verified: BOM-prefixed '# Title' now extracted both via FILE arg and stdin, byte-exact od -c evidence; mid-file BOM correctly NOT stripped; no-BOM content byte-identical.

title: Fence closing diverges from CommonMark: info-string closers and shorter closers accepted
description:
QA re-test t_6b5e5c59 @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.5, Linux).

CLAIM TESTED: spec docs/specs/mdoutline.md 'Fences open/close on lines whose first non-space characters are three or more backticks or tildes (matching char)'. Spec language is loose on closer details; CommonMark 0.31 §Fenced code blocks is the reference standard for 'real-world Markdown'.

ACTUAL (two divergences, both in mdoutline.py:45-64):
1) A closing fence may not carry an info string. 'mdoutline' treats '\`\`\`python' as closing an open backtick fence — CommonMark says it does NOT close (it is a content line). Content after it is parsed as Markdown.
   REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['# Doc','\`\`\`','\`\`\`python','# comment inside example','\`\`\`','# After']))"
   -> [(1,'Doc'), (1,'comment inside example')]   (expected only Doc, After)

2) Closing fence must be at least as long as the opener. Implementation closes a '\`\`\`\`' (4-backtick) fence on '\`\`\`' (3) — CommonMark requires closer >= opener length.
   REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['# Doc','\`\`\`\`','# inner','\`\`\`','# still inner per CommonMark','\`\`\`\`','# After']))"
   -> [(1,'Doc'), (1,'still inner per CommonMark')]   (expected only Doc, After)

Both affect real-world notes: fenced examples that embed a bare-fence line inside a longer fence (very common in Markdown tool documentation). Outcome is over-suppression (headings dropped from the outline) — wrong outline, not a crash.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — edge case, no data loss, workaround is editing the note. Overlaps in spirit with prior bead mdoutline-3o7 (CommonMark divergence in heading-close parsing) but is a distinct code path (fence-close validation vs heading text strip).

FIX HINT: when in_fence, require closer to have same char, count >= 3, count >= opener_count, and no non-space trailing content (info-string check).

NOTE: no epic bead exists in this repo's beads DB — no parent to link. Origin card: t_6b5e5c59.

title: Trailing-# stripping ignores CommonMark closing-sequence rule: '## C#' loses its '#'
description:
QA re-test t_543b747a @ 9083542 (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

CLAIM TESTED: spec 'trailing closing #s are stripped from the text' — implementation must only strip #s that form a CommonMark closing sequence (preceded by a space/tab).

ACTUAL: extract_headings strips ANY trailing #s plus preceding whitespace, no space required.
- '## C#'  -> (2, 'C')    expected (2, 'C#')
- '# foo#' -> (1, 'foo')  expected (1, 'foo#')
- '## T##' -> (2, 'T')    expected (2, 'T##')

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['## C#']))"
-> [(2, 'C')]

IMPACT: headings about C#/F# or ending in # lose characters. mdoutline.py:96-106 strips trailing #s unconditionally (the while loops never check for a whitespace boundary before the hash run). Unit tests only cover the space-separated variants (tests/test_mdoutline.py: test_trailing_closing_hashes_stripped, test_trailing_hashes_with_whitespace_stripped), so this is untested territory, not a regression.

SEVERITY: Minor/P3 — cosmetic edge case, does not block shipping. Spec language is arguably ambiguous; CommonMark semantics say keep the #.

NOTE: no epic bead exists in this repo's beads DB (freshly initialized for this QA cycle) — no parent to link. Origin card: t_543b747a.

title: CLI: '-' not accepted as stdin alias (Unix convention gap)
description:
QA re-test t_64d567c7 @ 72f6be4 (Python 3.13, Linux, fresh venv editable install).

CLAIM (convention, not spec): Unix CLI convention — '-' as positional file argument means stdin (cat, grep, sort, etc.). Spec froze CLI as 'optional positional file argument' without mentioning '-', so this is a Note-severity convention gap, not a spec violation.

ACTUAL: mdoutline - attempts to open a literal file named '-':
  printf '# Hi\n' | mdoutline -
  -> mdoutline: cannot read '-': No such file or directory  (stderr, exit 1)

REPRO: printf '# Hi\n' | mdoutline - ; echo $?

Suggested batch: fold into the polish ticket with f5w/3o7/ijd/zpw (tab-separator, BOM, closing-seq, fence-closer rules).

title: Spec tighter than CommonMark: tab after # not accepted as heading separator
description:
QA re-test t_543b747a @ bfaf57e (Python 3.14.6, Linux).

OBSERVATION (spec feedback, not an implementation defect):
Stamped spec docs/specs/mdoutline.md says a heading is 1-6 # then 'a space or end of line'. Implementation follows this exactly: '#<TAB>Title' is rejected (not a heading).
CommonMark 0.31 (§ATX headings) accepts one space OR tab after the hashes. Real-world notes pasted from editors that expand to tabs would silently drop such headings.

REPRO: python3 -c "import mdoutline; print(mdoutline.extract_headings(['#\tTab sep', '## A']))"
-> [(2, 'A')]

Route: product-owner (spec decision — widen the spec or accept as-is). Implementation is spec-conformant; no code change warranted unless spec changes.
